passages.text: Who has believed our message? And to whom has the arm of the LORD been revealed?
passages.sermon:
The prophet Isaiah speaks about God's Servant.
God's Servant is humble and suffers.
God's Servant is not attractive or majestic.
God's Servant is rejected by people.
God's Servant carries our pain and sorrow.
Isaiah asks a question.
Who has believed our message?
To whom has the power of the LORD been shown?
passages.original: מִ֥י הֶאֱמִ֖ין לִשְׁמֻעָתֵ֑נוּ וּזְר֥וֹעַ יְהוָ֖ה עַל־ מִ֥י נִגְלָֽתָה׃

passages.text: He grew up before Him like a tender shoot, and like a root out of dry ground. He had no stately form or majesty to attract us, no beauty that we should desire Him.
passages.sermon:
The servant of the Lord grew up before God.
He grew up like a young plant.
He grew up like a root coming out of dry ground.
He had no special form.
He had no majesty.
He did not look impressive to us.
He had no beauty that made us want Him.
passages.original: וַיַּ֨עַל כַּיּוֹנֵ֜ק לְפָנָ֗יו וְכַשֹּׁ֙רֶשׁ֙ מֵאֶ֣רֶץ צִיָּ֔ה לֹא־ תֹ֥אַר ל֖וֹ וְלֹ֣א הָדָ֑ר וְנִרְאֵ֥הוּ וְלֹֽא־ מַרְאֶ֖ה וְנֶחְמְדֵֽהוּ׃

passages.text: He was despised and rejected by men, a man of sorrows, acquainted with grief. Like one from whom men hide their faces, He was despised, and we esteemed Him not.
passages.sermon:
This passage describes the servant of the Lord.
He was despised by people.
People rejected Him.
He was a man who felt deep sorrow.
He knew pain and suffering well.
People turned away from Him.
They hid their faces from Him.
He was despised.
We did not value Him.
passages.original: נִבְזֶה֙ וַחֲדַ֣ל אִישִׁ֔ים אִ֥ישׁ מַכְאֹב֖וֹת וִיד֣וּעַ חֹ֑לִי וּכְמַסְתֵּ֤ר פָּנִים֙ מִמֶּ֔נּוּ נִבְזֶ֖ה וְלֹ֥א חֲשַׁבְנֻֽהוּ׃

passages.text: Surely He took on our infirmities and carried our sorrows; yet we considered Him stricken by God, struck down and afflicted.
passages.sermon:
He took our sicknesses.
He carried our sorrows.
We thought God punished Him.
We saw Him as struck down.
We believed He was afflicted.
passages.original: אָכֵ֤ן חֳלָיֵ֙נוּ֙ ה֣וּא נָשָׂ֔א וּמַכְאֹבֵ֖ינוּ סְבָלָ֑ם וַאֲנַ֣חְנוּ חֲשַׁבְנֻ֔הוּ נָג֛וּעַ מֻכֵּ֥ה אֱלֹהִ֖ים וּמְעֻנֶּֽה׃

passages.text: But He was pierced for our transgressions, He was crushed for our iniquities; the punishment that brought us peace was upon Him, and by His stripes we are healed.
passages.sermon:
He is the servant of the Lord.
He was pierced because of our transgressions.
He was crushed because of our iniquities.
God placed the punishment for our peace upon Him.
His wounds heal us.
passages.original: וְהוּא֙ מְחֹלָ֣ל מִפְּשָׁעֵ֔נוּ מְדֻכָּ֖א מֵעֲוֺנֹתֵ֑ינוּ מוּסַ֤ר שְׁלוֹמֵ֙נוּ֙ עָלָ֔יו וּבַחֲבֻרָת֖וֹ נִרְפָּא־ לָֽנוּ׃

passages.text: We all like sheep have gone astray, each one has turned to his own way; and the LORD has laid upon Him the iniquity of us all.
passages.sermon:
All people have wandered from God.
We are like sheep that have lost their way.
Each person has chosen his own path.
The LORD placed all our sins on Him.
passages.original: כֻּלָּ֙נוּ֙ כַּצֹּ֣אן תָּעִ֔ינוּ אִ֥ישׁ לְדַרְכּ֖וֹ פָּנִ֑ינוּ וַֽיהוָה֙ הִפְגִּ֣יעַ בּ֔וֹ אֵ֖ת עֲוֺ֥ן כֻּלָּֽנוּ׃

passages.text: He was oppressed and afflicted, yet He did not open His mouth. He was led like a lamb to the slaughter, and as a sheep before her shearers is silent, so He did not open His mouth.
passages.sermon:
He was oppressed.
He was afflicted.
He did not open His mouth.
People led Him like a lamb to the slaughter.
He was silent like a sheep before its shearers.
He did not open His mouth.
passages.original: נִגַּ֨שׂ וְה֣וּא נַעֲנֶה֮ וְלֹ֣א יִפְתַּח־ פִּיו֒ כַּשֶּׂה֙ לַטֶּ֣בַח יוּבָ֔ל וּכְרָחֵ֕ל לִפְנֵ֥י גֹזְזֶ֖יהָ נֶאֱלָ֑מָה וְלֹ֥א יִפְתַּ֖ח פִּֽיו׃

passages.text: By oppression and judgment He was taken away, and who can recount His descendants? For He was cut off from the land of the living; He was stricken for the transgression of My people.
passages.sermon:
God’s righteous Servant suffered.
People oppressed Him.
People judged Him unfairly.
They took Him away.
No one spoke about His descendants.
They cut Him off from the land of the living.
He died because of My people’s sin.
He was punished for their wrongdoing.
passages.original: מֵעֹ֤צֶר וּמִמִּשְׁפָּט֙ לֻקָּ֔ח וְאֶת־ דּוֹר֖וֹ מִ֣י יְשׂוֹחֵ֑חַ כִּ֤י נִגְזַר֙ מֵאֶ֣רֶץ חַיִּ֔ים מִפֶּ֥שַׁע עַמִּ֖י נֶ֥גַע לָֽמוֹ׃

passages.text: He was assigned a grave with the wicked, and with a rich man in His death, although He had done no violence, nor was any deceit in His mouth.
passages.sermon:
This passage describes the Righteous Servant of the Lord.
He was assigned a grave with wicked people.
He was with a rich man in His death.
He had done no violence.
He had no deceit in His mouth.
passages.original: וַיִּתֵּ֤ן אֶת־ רְשָׁעִים֙ קִבְר֔וֹ וְאֶת־ עָשִׁ֖יר בְּמֹתָ֑יו עַ֚ל לֹא־ חָמָ֣ס עָשָׂ֔ה וְלֹ֥א מִרְמָ֖ה בְּפִֽיו׃

passages.text: Yet it was the LORD’s will to crush Him and to cause Him to suffer; and when His soul is made a guilt offering, He will see His offspring, He will prolong His days, and the good pleasure of the LORD will prosper in His hand.
passages.sermon:
The LORD chose to crush His Servant.
The LORD caused His Servant to suffer.
The LORD made His Servant’s soul a guilt offering.
The Servant will see His offspring.
The Servant will live many days.
The LORD’s purpose will succeed through the Servant.
passages.original: וַיהוָ֞ה חָפֵ֤ץ דַּכְּאוֹ֙ הֶֽחֱלִ֔י אִם־ תָּשִׂ֤ים אָשָׁם֙ נַפְשׁ֔וֹ יִרְאֶ֥ה זֶ֖רַע יַאֲרִ֣יךְ יָמִ֑ים וְחֵ֥פֶץ יְהוָ֖ה בְּיָד֥וֹ יִצְלָֽח׃

passages.text: After the anguish of His soul, He will see the light of life and be satisfied. By His knowledge My righteous Servant will justify many, and He will bear their iniquities.
passages.sermon:
God has a righteous Servant.
This Servant suffers deep anguish in His soul.
After His suffering, the Servant sees the light of life.
He feels satisfied.
The Servant has great knowledge.
By His knowledge, the Servant justifies many people.
The Servant bears the sins of many people.
passages.original: מֵעֲמַ֤ל נַפְשׁוֹ֙ יִרְאֶ֣ה יִשְׂבָּ֔ע בְּדַעְתּ֗וֹ יַצְדִּ֥יק צַדִּ֛יק עַבְדִּ֖י לָֽרַבִּ֑ים וַעֲוֺנֹתָ֖ם ה֥וּא יִסְבֹּֽל׃

passages.text: Therefore I will allot Him a portion with the great, and He will divide the spoils with the strong, because He has poured out His life unto death, and He was numbered with the transgressors. Yet He bore the sin of many and made intercession for the transgressors.
passages.sermon:
God speaks about His righteous Servant.
God will give Him a share among the great.
He will divide the spoils with the strong.
He poured out His life to death.
He was counted with the sinners.
He carried the sin of many people.
He prayed for those who broke God’s law.
passages.original: לָכֵ֞ן אֲחַלֶּק־ ל֣וֹ בָרַבִּ֗ים וְאֶת־ עֲצוּמִים֮ יְחַלֵּ֣ק שָׁלָל֒ תַּ֗חַת אֲשֶׁ֨ר הֶעֱרָ֤ה לַמָּ֙וֶת֙ נַפְשׁ֔וֹ וְאֶת־ פֹּשְׁעִ֖ים נִמְנָ֑ה וְהוּא֙ חֵטְא־ רַבִּ֣ים נָשָׂ֔א וְלַפֹּשְׁעִ֖ים יַפְגִּֽיעַ׃ס
